```{r}
#| label: setup
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(targets)

summary_tables <- tar_read(imputation_summary)
levels_all <- tar_read(imputation_levels_all)
units_all <- tar_read(imputation_units_all)
settings <- tar_read(settings)

fmt <- function(x) format(round(x), big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 10))
options(knitr.kable.NA = "")
```

Missing covariates are imputed within each unit (dataset by wave by country), and missing screen use within each unit for each outcome's own model, `r settings$imputations` times while the engine is developed and 50 times for the confirmatory run.
A variable is imputed only where it is known for at least `r 100 * settings$impute_min_observed`% of the unit's rows, and for a child only where it is known for at least `r 100 * settings$impute_min_observed_age`% of the unit's children of the same age in whole years.
Outcomes are read by the imputation models and never imputed.
Every dataset's imputations passed the hard checks in `review_imputation()`, or the build would have stopped.

## What was imputed

One line per covariate and what became of its missing values, over all units with any.
Cells are counted once, not once per imputation.

```{r}
#| label: variables
summary_tables$variables |>
  transmute(
    Variable = variable,
    Outcome = outcome,
    Datasets = datasets,
    Units = fmt(units),
    `Cells missing` = fmt(cells_missing),
    `Cells imputed` = fmt(cells_imputed),
    `Left: age group not asked` = fmt(cells_age_group)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "llrrrrr")
```

```{r}
#| label: failures
failed <- units_all[
  !units_all$status %in% "imputed" &
    !grepl("^too little|^fewer rows|^not needed|^takes one", units_all$status),
]
```

`r nrow(failed)` unit and variable pairs failed or were only partly imputed.

```{r}
#| label: failures-table
failed |>
  count(dataset_id, variable, status, name = "units") |>
  knitr::kable()
```

## Imputed against observed covariates

An imputed value is one its unit observed, or one recorded for the same child at another wave.
Imputed values need not have the same distribution as observed ones: they differ where the children with a missing value differ from the rest.
A large gap is still worth a look.

The share of each category among observed and imputed values, pooled over datasets.

```{r}
#| label: levels
levels_all |>
  summarise(n = sum(n), .by = c(variable, source, level)) |>
  mutate(share = n / sum(n), .by = c(variable, source)) |>
  select(variable, level, source, share) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = source, values_from = share) |>
  filter(coalesce(observed, 0) >= 0.02 | coalesce(imputed, 0) >= 0.02) |>
  arrange(variable, desc(observed)) |>
  transmute(
    Variable = variable,
    Category = level,
    `Observed (%)` = round(100 * observed, 1),
    `Imputed (%)` = round(100 * imputed, 1)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "llrr")
```

Categories under 2% of both are not shown.

## What imputation changes for the models

The slopes of the development cells fitted on complete cases and on imputed data, by covariate tier.

```{r}
#| label: gain
summary_tables$gain |>
  transmute(
    Tier = tier,
    `Adjusted for other screen use` = ifelse(adjusted_other, "Yes", ""),
    `Slopes, complete cases` = fmt(slopes_complete),
    `Slopes, imputed` = fmt(slopes_imputed),
    `Datasets, complete cases` = datasets_complete,
    `Datasets, imputed` = datasets_imputed,
    `Rows, complete cases` = fmt(rows_complete),
    `Rows, imputed` = fmt(rows_imputed),
    `Fitted in some imputations only` = slopes_partly_fitted
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "r")
```

A slope fitted in only some imputations is not carried forward.

## How much information is missing

The fraction of information missing for a unit's slope: roughly the share of its variance that comes from not knowing the imputed values.
It also rises where a slope has few degrees of freedom, so a unit with few clusters can show a large fraction with little imputed.

```{r}
#| label: fmi
summary_tables$fmi |>
  transmute(
    Tier = tier,
    `Adjusted for other screen use` = ifelse(adjusted_other, "Yes", ""),
    Slopes = fmt(slopes),
    Datasets = datasets,
    `Nothing imputed` = fmt(nothing_imputed),
    `Median` = round(fmi_median, 3),
    `90th percentile` = round(fmi_q90, 3),
    `Largest` = round(fmi_max, 3),
    `Over a half` = fmi_over_half,
    `Design differed between imputations` = design_varied
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "r")
```

## Imputed covariates in the adjusted models

The share of an adjusted model's rows with any of its tier's covariates imputed.
Sex is not counted: it is in every model.
It is recorded for every unit slope (`covariate_imputed_share`).

```{r}
#| label: covariate-share
summary_tables$fmi |>
  filter(tier > 1) |>
  transmute(
    Tier = tier,
    Slopes = fmt(slopes),
    `Median share imputed (%)` = round(100 * covariate_share_median, 1),
    `90th percentile (%)` = round(100 * covariate_share_q90, 1),
    `Largest (%)` = round(100 * covariate_share_max, 1)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "r")
```

## Imputed screen use

Screen use is imputed for one model at a time, from a model that holds that model's outcome, so it is not stored.
The table counts the slopes that had any screen use imputed, and the share of their rows it was imputed for.

```{r}
#| label: exposure
summary_tables$fmi |>
  transmute(
    Tier = tier,
    `Adjusted for other screen use` = ifelse(adjusted_other, "Yes", ""),
    Slopes = fmt(slopes),
    `With screen use imputed` = fmt(exposure_imputed),
    `Draw failed, rows left out` = exposure_failed,
    `Median share of rows imputed (%)` = round(100 * exposure_share_median, 1),
    `Largest share (%)` = round(100 * exposure_share_max, 1)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "r")
```

With `r settings$imputations` imputations these fractions are themselves rough; they settle with 50.
